nodes.description: OER LSV performance comparison of all catalysts in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: the Ni-FeNH present the best OER activity (Figure 2a), with a lower overpotential of 224, 303 and 352 mV to drive the large current density of 100, 500 and 800 mA cm⁻², respectively.

nodes.description: OER stability at 500 mA/cm² in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: the Ni-FeNH present stable OER activity at an industrial-level current density of 500 mA cm⁻² for 500 hours, and the overpotential only approximately 30 mV increase.

nodes.description: Industrial water electrolysis with 30% KOH at 80°C
nodes.source_text: the Ni-FeNH need 1.85 V to drive the industrial-level current density of 400 mA cm⁻², corresponding to the energy consumption of 4.42 kWh m⁻³ H₂. Remarkably, the required voltage of the Ni-FeNH dropped by 39 mV compared to pure Ni mesh... the Ni-FeNH can operated stably at the large current of 8000 mA ... for 100 hours

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of Ni-FeNH exhibit similar diffraction peaks with Fe₂O(OH)₃NO₃·H₂O PDF#01-089-6191.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1b, the X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of Ni-FeNH exhibits similar diffraction peaks with Fe₂O(OH)₃NO₃·H₂O PDF#01-089-6191

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern shows three rings with spacing of 0.150, 0.214 and 0.250 nm belonging to (045), (042) and (004) planes of Fe₂O(OH)₃NO₃·H₂O.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the three rings with a spacing of 0.150, 0.214 and 0.250 nm are belonged to the (045), (042) and (004) planes of the Fe₂O(OH)₃NO₃·H₂O (Figure 1c), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images reveal Ni-FeNH present thin and dense nanosheets growing on nickel foam.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images reveal that Ni-FeNH present thin and dense nanosheets growing on nickel foam (Figure S5a-c).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images show obvious crystalline phase inlaid in amorphous phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images show that obvious crystalline phase was inlaid in amorphous phase

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows crystalline phase with lattice distance of 0.208 and 0.244 nm corresponding to (044) and (004) planes of Fe₂O(OH)₃NO₃·H₂O.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images show that obvious crystalline phase was inlaid in amorphous phase, in which crystalline phase present lattice distance of 0.208 and 0.244 nm (Figure S5d), corresponding to (044) and (004) planes of the Fe₂O(OH)₃NO₃·H₂O separately.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mapping images show Fe, Ni, O and N elements were uniform spatial distributions throughout the thin nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe, Ni, O and N elements were uniform spatial distributions throughout the thin nanosheets (Figure 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman peaks at 313, 468, 542, 683 and 1050 cm⁻¹ assigned to O-H group, Ni²⁺-O bending, Fe/Ni (oxy)hydroxide stretching, amorphous FeOOH and NO₃⁻ vibration; peak at 1050 cm⁻¹ shows slight red shift.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman peaks of the Ni-FeNH at 313, 468, 542, 683 and 1050 cm⁻¹, which can be assigned to hydroxyl (O-H) group, Ni²⁺-O bending mode, Fe/Ni (oxy) hydroxide stretching vibration, Fe-O vibration (amorphous FeOOH) and NO₃⁻ vibration, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-IR spectra show absorption bands at 1355 cm⁻¹ confirming existence of NO₃⁻ in Ni-FeNH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectra (Figure S7), the absorption bands located at 1355 cm⁻¹, further confirming the existence of NO₃⁻ in Ni-FeNH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe 2p XPS spectra negatively shift 0.8 eV and Ni 2p positively shift 0.6 eV compared to Ni-FeOOH, indicating strong electron interaction; Ni-FeNH exhibited highest Ni²⁺ ratio among all samples; N 1s peak at 406.6 eV corresponds to N-O band of NO₃⁻.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with the Ni-FeOOH, the Fe 2p XPS spectra of Ni-FeNH negatively shift with 0.8 eV (Figure 1e), while the binding energies of Ni 2p have a positive shift of 0.6 eV (Figure 1f), suggesting that NO₃⁻ embedded Fe(Ni) oxyhydroxides network brought a strong electron interaction between Fe and Ni ion... But should not be ignored is that Ni-FeNH exhibited the highest ratio of Ni²⁺ among all samples (Table S2)... the peak at 406.6 eV in N 1s XPS spectra correspond to the N-O band of NO₃⁻ (Figure 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP shows Fe/Ni ions leached from Ni-FeNH are lower than NiFe-LDH, Ni-FeOOH and Ni(OH)₂/FeOOH at 500 mA cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, the inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP) was carried out to evaluate the stability of Fe and Ni atom in Ni-FeNH during sharp OER process. Apparently, the Fe/Ni ions leached from Ni-FeNH are lower than that of NiFe-LDH, Ni-FeOOH and Ni(OH)₂/FeOOH at the current density of 500 mA cm⁻² (Figure 2e)
